record.paper_title: Completeness of sets of complex exponentials in convex sets: open problems
record.original_question: Let Λ = {λ_n} be a sequence of pairwise distinct complex numbers with 0 not in Λ and λ_n tending to infinity, and let Exp Λ = {exp(λ_n z)}. Let K be a compact convex set in the complex plane with nonempty interior, and let H(K) be the space of continuous complex-valued functions on K that are holomorphic in the interior and carry the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets. What precise condition characterizes exactly when Exp Λ is complete in H(K)?

evidence.quote: Let Λ = {λ_n}, n ∈ N, be a sequence of pairwise different complex numbers (points) in the complex plane C, 0 ∉ Λ, and λ_n → ∞ as n → +∞. Let X be a convex open or closed set on C. By H(X) denote the space of all continuous complex-valued functions on X which are holomorpic in the interior Int X of X (if Int X ≠ ∅) with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of X. An exponential system Exp Λ = {exp(λ_n z)} is complete in X if the closure of the linear span of Exp Λ in H(X) coincides with H(X).
6) X = K, where K is a compact convex set in C, Int K ≠ ∅.

(6-?) No precise condition is known for the completeness of systems Exp Λ in K. The completeness problem in K is apparently a very difficult problem (cf. with X = [-a,a]). We present a test for the completeness of systems Exp Λ in K to within two exponentials.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Lambda=\{\lambda_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of pairwise distinct complex numbers with $0\notin\Lambda$ and $\lambda_n\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$. Define the exponential system $\operatorname{Exp}\Lambda=\{e^{\lambda_n z}\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$. Let $K\subset\mathbb{C}$ be a compact convex set with nonempty interior $\operatorname{Int} K$, and let $H(K)$ denote the space of all continuous complex-valued functions on $K$ that are holomorphic in $\operatorname{Int} K$, endowed with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of $K$. The system $\operatorname{Exp}\Lambda$ is said to be complete in $H(K)$ if the closure of its linear span in $H(K)$ equals $H(K)$.

Problem: Find a precise necessary and sufficient condition, expressed in terms of the distribution of the points of $\Lambda$ and the geometry of $K$, for $\operatorname{Exp}\Lambda$ to be complete in $H(K)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature describes the completeness problem for exponential systems on a general compact convex set $K\subset\mathbb{C}$ with nonempty interior as a long-standing open problem. Only partial results (sufficient conditions, stability results generalizing the Redheffer–Alexander theorem for an interval, and tests for completeness up to finitely many exponentials) are available, and no precise characterization is known.

status_evidence.title: Stability of Completeness for Systems of Exponentials on Compact Convex Sets in ℂ
status_evidence.snippet: A sufficient condition for the stability of completeness of systems of exponentials in spaces of functions continuous on and holomorphic inside a compact convex set in C with nonempty interior is obtained, generalizing the Redheffer–Alexander result for the interval.
status_evidence.claim: Only sufficient/stability conditions are known; no exact characterization for general compact convex K.

status_evidence.title: A problem on completeness of exponentials
status_evidence.snippet: Completeness problems for exponential systems remain a topic of active research with partial results in special cases.
status_evidence.claim: The completeness problem for exponentials on general convex sets is studied with only partial answers.
